Application Materials.content:
- A **500-word personal statement** should include your reasons for choosing the course, the modules/areas of study you are particularly interested in, the skills and knowledge you are hoping to gain, and a demonstration of your relevant skills and experience.
- You’ll need to upload certain documents as part of the application process. These include:
- Transcripts of your qualifications
- English language test certificates if taken
- Personal statement (if not written directly into the portal)
- Scholarship documentation (if applying)
- If you don’t have all of your documents when you apply, you can upload them later through the portal.

Application Deadlines.content: Most postgraduate courses start in September or October. For some courses there may be alternative starts dates, for example in January or April. Applications can normally be submitted all year round and open in the October of the year preceding the start of your course. Durham normally requires applicants who require a student visa to apply for their postgraduate programme by **the end of July** and applicants who do not require a student visa to apply by **the end of August**. Offer holders should supply evidence to meet offer conditions normally no later than **mid-August** if a student visa is needed and **mid-September** if not. The University can close admissions to any programme if it becomes over-subscribed.

Academic Requirements.content:
- The MSc in Business Analytics programme is designed for graduates from either **a business background (with evidence of strong quantitative content)** or **a tech background (including numerate scientific disciplines with strong computational content)**.
- Applicants need **a UK first or upper second class honours degree or international equivalent** in one of the following: **Business; Computer science; Related subject with a strong quantitative component**.
- For applicants from China: **a standard full-time bachelor’s degree (4 years minimum), with a minimum average grade of between 75% - 85% from a recognised prestigious university**. Applicants from **non-prestigious institution** with **a minimum grade of 90% or above** will be considered on a case-by-case basis.

Program Overview.content:
The MSc in Business Analytics equips you with cutting-edge skills in AI, data science, and decision-making, empowering you to turn big data into strategic business insights and drive innovation, efficiency, and competitive advantage in today’s data-driven world.
Course details: Degree type: MSc; Course code: G5K709; Course length: 1 year full-time; Start date: [September 2026](https://www.durham.ac.uk/business/courses/business-analytics-g5k709/september-2026/).
Our MSc in Business Analytics will equip you with the skills and knowledge to harness AI-driven analytics for gaining competitive business insights from big data. With businesses increasingly relying on Artificial Intelligence and advanced analytics to understand and predict customer behaviour, optimise internal processes, and manage suppliers effectively, this programme prepares you to navigate and lead in this data-driven world.
In a supportive, research-led learning environment, you will explore the complexities of big data, machine learning, and natural language processing, applying cutting-edge AI techniques to extract key insights and drive strategic decision-making. You will benefit from the programme’s strong international connections and gain hands-on experience with AI-powered analytics on the [**International Field Trip**](https://www.durham.ac.uk/business/programmes/masters/business-analytics-international-field-trip/). A key part of your studies, where you can turn your learning into action, is the [**Business Analytics Project**](https://www.durham.ac.uk/business/programmes/masters/business-analytics-projects/) - a unique opportunity to tackle real-world business challenges using data-driven insights. Additionally, you will have the opportunity to engage with industry leaders and renowned scholars through Business School presentations, featuring major global multinationals and leading academic experts.
Delivered full-time over one year, the programme is led by the **Department of Computer Science** and co-delivered and co-managed with the **Business School**, combining expertise from both departments to provide a well-rounded education in AI-driven business analytics. The Business School is one of the longest established in the UK, with a reputation for academic excellence and state-of-the-art learning facilities. It is also one of an elite group of institutions in the UK to be accredited by all three major business education accreditation bodies: the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB), the Association of MBAs (AMBA) and the European Quality Improvement System (EQUIS). The Department of Computer Science is ranked 11th out of 117 universities in the Complete University Guide 2026.
World class Business Education: **50th in the World** - QS Global Business Masters Rankings 2026: Business Analytics.
Your MSc Business Analytics programme consists of a set of core modules beginning with an in-depth understanding and introduction to Business Analytics, through to modules that will provide you with an appreciation of, and the ability to apply, a range of predictive and prescriptive business analytics techniques. A highlight of the programme is the International Field Trip, with the programme culminating in the Business Analytics Project.
As part of the programme, you will be encouraged to attend presentations by leading academics and professionals who are specialists in your particular area of interest. Past speakers have included representatives of major global multinationals and leading scholars, combining critical and progressive thinking with practical insights.
The course is taught through a mixture of lectures, seminars and practicals as well as the requirement to complete a major dissertation. There is also a major International Field trip, which takes place in the third term. Practicals are medium sized group sessions, where you will practice computer software, applying topics from lectures and seminars.
The Business Analytics Project makes up one-third of your marks and is assessed through a 15,000-word document that tests your acquisition of relevant subject-specific knowledge and skills and your ability to apply these, and appropriate key skills, in the context of a Masters-level research project.
You will be taught at our Business School, Waterside. This additional building will complement our current Mill Hill Lane site, and both sites will deliver a world-class business teaching and learning experience. Waterside is nestled in the heart of Durham City Centre, just a few minutes walk from the railway station, along the scenic banks of the River Wear.
The Department of Computer Science’s academic fusion of technology and independent thinking places it firmly at the cutting edge of computer learning. Learning from academics who lead cutting-edge research provides valuable insight into high quality projects, and gives our postgraduate community the opportunity to play a role in shaping a future in which crucial developments in society are supported by technological innovation. Researchers in the Department offer a range of expertise across the computer science spectrum in areas such as artificial intelligence, data science, bioinformatics, high-performance computing, graphics and fundamental algorithms. The Department keeps close links with local high-technology industries as well as national and international employers.
Our postgraduate programmes with a focus on employability fully equip you with the skills and industry insight to embark on a successful and rewarding business career. You gain a combination of analytical and practical skills that employers value, such as independent thinking and problem-solving, and are able to enhance your people skills that are essential in business and much sought after by employers.

Curriculum.content:
Course length: **1 year full-time**.
Delivered full-time over one year, the MSc Business Analytics programme is led by the **Department of Computer Science** and co-delivered and co-managed with the **Business School**.
The programme consists of a set of core modules beginning with an in-depth understanding and introduction to Business Analytics, through to modules that provide an appreciation of, and the ability to apply, a range of predictive and prescriptive business analytics techniques. A highlight of the programme is the International Field Trip, with the programme culminating in the Business Analytics Project.
Core modules:
- Introduction to Business Analytics
- Data Analytics in Action
- Learning from Data
- Managing Data Driven Innovation
- Natural Language Analysis
- Retail Analytics
- Data Analytics for Strategic Decision-Making
- Data Analytics in Action - International Field Trip
- Business Analytics Project
The International Field Trip aims to provide experiential learning needed to acquire an inside perspective of operating globally. Students visit a series of data-intensive participating organisations, analyse each organisation using a structured learning approach, and present their analysis to representatives of the participating organisations.
The Business Analytics Project requires an in-depth investigation into an issue applicable and relevant to business analytics, underpinned by business analytics approaches, methods and techniques covered in the other modules. Students choose a project either by working with a host organisation or by producing an issue-led investigation, and the project is supervised by a faculty member.
The course is taught through a mixture of lectures, seminars and practicals as well as the requirement to complete a major dissertation. There is also a major International Field Trip, which takes place in the third term.
Assessment includes written assignments and combinations of written assignments and individual and group presentations. The Business Analytics Project makes up **one-third of your marks** and is assessed through a **15,000-word document**.

Cost of Attendance.content:
- Travel: unlimited travel throughout the day on Arriva bus services within the Durham District Zone is available for **£1.50 per day** with a valid campus ID card. A 16-25 railcard can be purchased for **£30**; the rail fare between Durham City and Newcastle is around **£6.00**.
- Keeping in touch: a mobile phone contract typically costs between **£10 and £50 a month** depending on the type of phone and allowance.
- Entertainment: cinema tickets from **£5** at the Gala Theatre; Durham Student Theatre tickets for students approx. **£6**; a meal out can be as little as **£5-10** with student discounts, with a standard meal out around **£5-10** for a starter, **£10-15** for the main course, and around **£5** for a dessert; Lane 7 Bowling approximately **£7** with a valid [NUS](https://www.nus.org.uk/) card.

Financial Aid.content:
Our Master in Business Analytics Scholarships celebrates and rewards exceptional candidates applying to the programme. To apply you must submit an application form and hold an offer for the programme by one of the deadlines below.
| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Amount** | Up to **£12,000** off tuition fees |
| **Year of Entry** | Applicants for programmes commencing in 2026/27 |
| **Number of awards available** | 10 |
| **Level of study** | Postgraduate |
| **Mode of study** | Full-time |
| **Programmes** | MSc Business Analytics |
| **Duration** | Scholarship (tuition fee discount) covers the standard completion timescales of our programmes. Scholarships will be applied as a discount against the full tuition fee for the programme. |
**Eligibility:** Scholarships (tuition fee discounts) will be awarded to offer holders based on the following eligibility criteria:
- Demonstrate an outstanding academic record from a recognised and reputable institution.
- Demonstrate the potential to contribute and enrich all aspects of the Masters programme and the diverse academic and cultural profile of the Masters class.
- Have the potential to become an exemplary alumni ambassador, contributing positively to the School, to professional organisations, and to the wider community.
**How to Apply**
- Hold a formal offer for the MSc Business Analytics programme.
- Complete the [**MSc Business Analytics Scholarship Application**](https://forms.office.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=i9hQcmhLKUW-RNWaLYpvlLj1iWQACOJMoA7EciJSOtRURUk2RlNCQVNEMTcwVkxSNllJTk42UThTNS4u) by: 1st round selection: midnight (GMT) **2 March 2026**; 2nd round selection: midnight (GMT) **1 May 2026**.
**Terms and Conditions:** Applicants must:
- Be **completely self-funding** to be eligible for this tuition fee discount. Where fees are paid by an employer, private provider or government body applicants will not be considered for a scholarship. Failure to disclose external funding will invalidate any scholarship offering.
- If you are in receipt of another Durham University tuition discount (e.g. Inspiring Excellence) you can apply for this scholarship, but they can not be combined if you are successful.
- Complete the appropriate programme application process in full and be in receipt of an offer before the application deadlines. If you do not hold an offer you will not be considered for an award.
- Be available to take up their programme place in the 2026 academic year.
**Only successful candidates will be notified.** This will be via email within 10 working days of the application deadline. Scholarships are not transferable and not deferrable. They are valid only for use by scholarship winners in the academic year for which the scholarship has been awarded. **Scholarship (tuition fee discount) decisions are at the discretion of the School and all decisions are final.**

Multiple Applications.content: You can apply for as many Masters Programmes as you choose. Applicants can receive two or more offers, but can accept only one. Once an offer is accepted, any other applications will be automatically declined.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
Durham University is able to consider a **Change of year** on a case-by-case basis. You can request a change through your Applicant Portal homepage. Durham is not able to approve all requests, but if approved you will receive a new offer letter in your Applicant Portal.
If you request a deferral, your application will be deferred and reconsidered when the next admissions cycle opens. You can only defer **one year at a time** (for example from 2026 to 2027 - not 2028). If you are unable to take up your place following a deferral, you will need to submit a new application in the next cycle.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
This policy applies to all applications for postgraduate taught (PGT) courses at Durham University.
- If an applicant misses the English Language requirement, they may become eligible to undertake a **Pre-sessional Academic English course**, in which case the results from this course would then be used as evidence to satisfy the English Language requirement. Admissions teams will signpost applicants to pre-sessional courses and assess eligibility based on the results of an applicant’s latest English Language Test.
- Once an applicant receives their results, these should be sent to the University for consideration via the PG Applicant Portal for postgraduate taught courses. If **all the conditions of an applicant’s offer are fully satisfied**, then a place is guaranteed on their chosen course.
- If any of the **academic or English language conditions** of the offer are missed, the decision to accept or reject the applicant remains at the discretion of the University. In some instances where academic conditions have not been met, Admissions experts may decide to offer a change of course to a similar programme where the applicant meets the entry criteria and there is space available.
- If an applicant does not meet the English language conditions of their offer, they may be offered the opportunity to complete a **Pre-sessional English Language course prior to the start of their main programme**.
- Applicants completing pre-sessional English Language courses will be required to pay a deposit for their main programme before a single or combined CAS is issued. If an applicant **does not pass the pre-sessional programme**, a deposit refund will not be granted.
